references.text: The same expression 'he judged Israel' is used of Othniel, the first judge, and points to the continuity of the office of judge.
Jephthah judged Israel for six years and was buried, following the same pattern regarding the duration of service and burial.
Ibzan judged Israel, died, and was buried, using an identical formula that describes the minor judges.
Elon judged Israel for ten years, died, and was buried, showing the same narrative structure for the minor judges.
Abdon judged Israel for eight years, died, and was buried, a parallel description of the period of judgment and death.
The preceding verse introduces Tola, who arose to save Israel and lived in Shamir, providing direct context.
